lines.en: I leave Makoto behind and start making my way home, equal parts exasperated and concerned.
For one, it’s relatively late and I have no idea whether or not Ami is even going to be awake by the time I get home.

On top of that, though, how is this going to make me sound? And why am I even concerned about how I’m going to sound in the first place when all that should really matter is the effect it will have on her?
She’ll know right away that this isn’t my idea. And I know her, so I know it will make her concerned about how I landed on this. And she knows me so she’ll know I’ll be concerned as a result of that.
Then, we can all be concerned together because that’s an important adjective beginning with the letter C (which rhymes with T) and I just want this day to be over.
Unfortunately, nothing ever ends when I want it to. It’s either long before or long after. Which means that either this night is going to last an extra several hours-
Or I am going to be hit by a car on the way home and Ami will be left with no one but a girl who only wants her because she shares my blood.
I used to buy books for Ami when she was much smaller.
I don’t know why I’m just now remembering that- but perhaps it has something to do with this door.
Come to think of it, there’s a verse that sticks out in my head when I look at it. But I can’t remember all of it, so I hope this much will do.
The hallway of life is door upon door.
Each door has a doorknob. Each opens to secrets.
One secret. One doorknob.
Daily, I choose a doorway to walk through.
At times I’m confused for I know that each door is a new day to live, a new way to struggle, a new way to give.
I stand in this hall lined with doors, doors galore, knowing each doorway will open to more-
Seeking the one that will make me feel free-
And turning a doorknob to find a new me...
That’s what I hope to get out of this, isn’t it?
Maybe not right away, but I wouldn’t be putting the effort in at all if I wasn’t in search of a change, right?
Is there a new me behind this door?
Is she playing patty-cake with him? Or dressing him up in women’s clothes as he scoffs and pretends he isn’t enjoying it?
Or is it simply locked?
: Ami?
Maybe I’ll get lucky.
Maybe it will be empty.
: Come in...
: Hey...sorry for bothering you so late.
: If you’re going to apologize to anyone, it should probably be Niki...I just got off the phone with her and she’s still mad about you leaving me alone.
: And besides, you don’t ever have to apologize to me, Sensei. Especially now that I’ve hurt you.
: It was barely a scratch, Ami. It healed within a few days.
: Do you want to hurt me to make up for it? Because you can if you want. I deserve it.
: I’m good. Do you have a few minutes to talk, though?
: I have all the time in the world. But what is it you want to talk about?
: A few things, actually. And one of them involves Niki. But chances are I’ll tuck my tail between my legs and escape before I can even get to that part.
: I’m...confused.
: Yeah...me too.
: But I’ve been confused a lot lately. And that’s not fair to you.
: ...Sensei?
: How long have you been stuck in here now?
: I...haven’t really been keeping track...
: Me neither. And that’s just one of the many pieces of evidence you can use to explain how absent I’ve been when you need me the most.
: But...that’s not true. You’ve been cleaning...kind of. And you’re cooking for me and-

: Microwaving food and picking up things from the convenience store doesn’t count as cooking. And despite you dedicating your entire life to caring for me, I’ve put in virtually no effort at all to return the favor.
: I’m not expecting you to return the favor, Sensei. I-
: Shut up and let me finish.

: I want to be a better guardian. But just wanting that is all I’ve been able to do so far. And each day I spend without taking another step in the right direction is another day in a hallway lined with locked doors.
: In a...hallway lined with...what? I don’t get it.
: You don’t have to get it. The point is, I need to do something. Something more than just wanting to do something or you’ll never leave this room.
: Is that what you want?
: Only if you’re stuck in here with me...
: I think I’ve made it pretty apparent with my actions in recent days that that’s not how things are going to be.
: I can’t sit still. I like ruining things too much.
: That’s just how it is for now...
: But one day, we’ll be in this same position again. And you won’t want to leave then.
: When that time comes, you’ll stay right here with me.
: We’ll grow old and die inside of this house, and no one will find us until we’re both decayed and covered in maggots.
: Sounds delightful. No thanks.
: I don’t want you to change, Sensei.
: Not even if it means being better?
: You can’t get any better than you are now. You’re perfect for me and I am perfect for you.
: I can get a lot better, Ami. I just...might need a little assistance in order to do that.
: Getting assistance from anyone else will just make you worse.
: Would it be worse if I could actually cook for you? If I knew what to buy you from the store and you didn’t have to call Niki because you don’t have any faith in me? Would that be worse, Ami?
: That alone? Of course not...
: But that’s not how it would go.
: Small changes lead to bigger changes. Then bigger changes lead to colossal ones. Then...something, something, butterfly effect.
: I don’t want that...
: I want my uncle...
: Would a father not be better?
: Move over. This isn’t a conversation we should have with me just standing here.
: Sensei...
: Move.
: I know you think you’ve failed me, but it’s the other way around. And I’m sorry I ever let things get to that point in the first place.
: I want you to be able to count on me. But I also know that counting on me in my current state would be nothing short of idiotic. And even you’re smarter than that.
: Are you...making fun of me?
: Yes. And I’m doing that because I can make fun of you and everything will be fine because that’s how strong our connection is. But even so, there’s something about it that needs to change.
: If I’m ever going to really be there for you, I need to figure out a place to start. And what better place than the middle of the woods?
: Let’s go on a trip. A camping trip, specifically.
: You...want to go...camping?...
: Yeah. I think it’ll be good for us to get out of the house for a little while. And your friends won’t be around to see you looking like a drowned rat in the middle of the woods.
: I...don’t understand.
: I want to be more like a parent to you, Ami. You’ve been deprived of a relationship like that for half of your life and that just isn’t fair.
: It’s no wonder you act so fucking insane all of the time. You never learned how to be normal because I was never there to teach you that.
: So you’re...going to teach me how to...put up a tent instead?
: Honestly, I have no idea how to do that myself.
: Then where the heck are we going to sleep in the middle of the woods?!
: We’ll figure it out. I just think we need a fresh start — and I think doing things we wouldn’t normally do otherwise is a...good way to commence that process.
: I mean...I don’t dislike the idea. It just...doesn’t seem like something you’d come up with on your own.
: What difference does it make if I’m the one who came up with it or not? The fact remains that I want to do this for you. And, to a lesser extent...myself, I guess.
: But, Sensei...I never went camping with my dad. How does doing that make you more like-
: Again, it doesn’t matter what it is. I’m sure an uncle could take his niece on a camping trip too. But I don’t think that’s what you want.
: And it might not even be how you look at me in the first place. I just know that, whatever I am to you, it’s not enough anymore.
: So, call me a jerk and interpret this however you like, but I want to fix you. And I want you to fix me. And we can’t do that if we stay the way we are now.
: We both need help, Ami. A lot of it. And we’re too stubborn to ever truly take that from someone else, so we need to rely on each other. Do you think you can do that?
: Of course I can do that. I’ve been doing that for half of my life. But why would you want to get any closer to me when you know how dangerous I am?
: You’re not dangerous, Ami.
: I cut your hand! I threatened all of the other girls at school! I went through your phone! I used it to blackmail people! I’m a bad girl, Sensei! And now you want to reward me for that?! Why?!

: Do you really think you’re the only person who’s “bad” here? Because I’ve done my fair share of terrible things as well. So how about we just say they cancel each other out and we can be horrible together?
: Would you really accept me as a daughter after how hard I’ve made everything for you?...
: Would you really accept me as a father after I waited for you to go bat-shit crazy before finally deciding to step up?
: This...is all really surprising to me, Sensei. I’m not sure how to react.
: Do you want to go camping or not? I have to know if I should pack your bag, because we’d be leaving in the morning.
: I’d go anywhere with you. I just...can’t help but shake the feeling that you just want to drop me off in the woods and leave me there to die.
: And if that’s what you want, fine. I’ll die. I just don’t want to get my hopes up and then immediately find out that none of this is real.
: Ami, look at me.
: I want you to have a happy life.
: And I will do whatever it takes to make that happen.
: I don’t need much, Sensei. Just you.
: Then you can have me. And I will build you a world where nothing can hurt you anymore.
: I’ll protect you with all I have, and keep you on the right path even though I can’t ever seem to travel down it myself.
: I will be exactly what I was meant to be all this time, and you’ll be able to breathe easy knowing that nothing you do will ever make me leave.
: You don’t mean that.
: I do.
: But what if it’s something really bad?
: We’ll cross that bridge when we come to it.
: What if I hurt you again?
: It’ll heal.
: What if it doesn’t?
: Then I’ll have a scar.
: But I don’t want you to have any more scars when you already have a million on the inside.
: And the same goes for how I feel about you. But that’s the point of this fresh start and why I’m going to try and be better.
: Just...please forgive me if I start proposing more things like this as I’ve become desperate enough to start taking suggestions since thinking is hard and I have lost all will to live.
: Will you really accept me, Sensei?
: Is that even a question? Of course.
: For better or for worse?
: I don’t think things can get much worse than this.
: In sickness and in health?
: Mostly sickness, I assume. But again, yes.
: I accept you, flaws and all. And I promise that, even when I can’t help but ruin things again in the future, I’ll remain by your side no matter what.
: You really mean that?
: I do.
: You deserve a proper home. And a proper home has more in it than one little girl and the space that I take up. A proper home has a family.
: But we’ve been family all along...that’s what I’m so confused about.
: In nothing but blood. You’ve carried the rest of this “family” on your back. And all I’m trying to do now is take a little of that weight off.
: You deserve to rest.
: So I will ask again-
: Yes.
: Yes?
: Yeah...I’ll go.
: But, fair warning...I have no idea what to do. And I’d kind of like to know who gave you this idea in the first place..
: I’ll tell you tomorrow. I have to pack our stuff, and you need to be getting to sleep as well.
: But, wait...wasn’t there something else that you wanted to-
: Yeah.
: I don’t have the energy for more than one step at a time, though.
: And I’m pretty sure that this one would make her proud enough to forgive me for forgoing the next.
: Camping, huh?...
: And who was he talking about just now?
: No, I don’t think it was you.
: But it could be fun. And he’s never called himself that before.
: You think so?
: And if it doesn’t work?...
: That’s easy.
: I can chop it off.
Ami’s affection has increased to [ami_love]!
